free_tier.stated: Reported as 5 NZB downloads and 25 API hits per day on the free 'Water' tier; Lager EUR 5/year gives 25 downloads and 250 API calls a day, Ale EUR 10/year 100 and 1,000, Wine EUR 20/year 200 and 2,000. The vendor's caps declares <limits max="100" default="100"/> and <registration available="yes" open="no"/>.
free_tier.notes: Free API allowance is disputed: usenetreviews.org and bestnzbsites say 100 hits/day, a 2023 registration thread says 25, and usenet.com says 'a small number'. The conservative 25 is kept.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an NZB pointer file

retention.stated: not stated by the vendor on any page reachable today; a third-party listing claims '3000+ days for binary'.

egress.terms: No byte metering; the API returns pointers.

interface_detail: Newznab API at /api; caps answers anonymously with 100 results per request. The HTML site is behind Cloudflare and returns 403 on every path tried (/, /register, /plans, /faq, /help, /support, /donate, /subscribe, /store), while /api answers normally.
tooling: Native Newznab: Prowlarr, NZBHydra2, Sonarr and Radarr add it with URL plus key once an account exists.
chaining: A depth index for older and rarer material behind a 5-grab-a-day free cap; it complements a broad index rather than replacing one.

limits.value: 5 NZB downloads and 25 API hits per day on the free tier

limits_note: The hard gate is registration, not the counter: nobody without an invite reaches the counter.
binding_note: The invite gate is what fails first, before any quota is reached: without an account the 5 grabs cannot be spent at all. If an account existed, the daily counter would bind instead.

identity_cost.detail: Invite only. The register page says 'Sorry! The Bar is closed. Please don't contact us asking for invites.' caps agrees: <registration available="yes" open="no"/>.

reliability_note: Registration opens for short windows and closes again, so an account is an asset that cannot be recreated on demand if lost.
confidence_note: Registration closure is documented from the vendor's own register page and caps. The free allowance is third-party, and the record's verdict does not depend on it.

evidence.proved: caps returned 200 and 3,247 bytes: title DS, <limits max="100" default="100"/>, <registration available="yes" open="no"/>
vendor text via search snippet: 'Sorry! The Bar is closed. Please don't contact us asking for invites.' The direct fetch of the page returned a Cloudflare 403.
HTML site returns 403 with a Cloudflare 'Attention Required' body (4,556 bytes); /api is unaffected
third-party tier table: Water free 5 NZBs; Lager 25/250 at EUR 5; Ale 100/1,000 at EUR 10; Wine 200/2,000 at EUR 20

notes: The /api path answering while every HTML path is challenged is itself the useful finding: an indexer the browser cannot open still exposes caps, so registration state and result limits are readable without an account.
